description: Looking for team members to build a lunar landing site navigator
summary:
What We Developed:
STELLARON is an interactive, physics-grounded lunar landing site navigator and mission rehearsal platform. Powered by Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LOLA 30m) digital elevation models and NASA SPICE (DE421) planetary ephemeris, it visualizes real-time solar illumination, Earth communication geometry, and 3D descent trajectories across 14 candidate lunar landing sites.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
The lunar south pole features extreme topography, perpetual crater shadows, and grazing solar angles. STELLARON addresses this by evaluating site survivability under operational launch slips. Through an integrated launch-delay calendar, physical horizon-masking engine, and battery state-of-charge simulation, it models the exact impact of mission slips across four sequential flight decision gates.

Why It Is Important:
A launch slip of only a few days can shift a landing site from continuous sunlight into freezing darkness, depleting battery reserves. STELLARON translates complex astrodynamic and topographic data into actionable visual trade-offs, enabling engineers, planners, and students to safeguard lander survival before flight.
details:
STELLARON — Project Details

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

STELLARON is an interactive, physics-grounded lunar landing site evaluation and mission rehearsal platform designed for the Artemis exploration era. It models the complex illumination, line-of-sight communication, and terrain hazards of the lunar south pole to evaluate whether a landing site remains viable when launch schedules slip.

How It Works Under the Hood:

  • Ephemeris Engine: Integrates NASA JPL SPICE planetary ephemeris (DE421 kernel) through sub-second numerical bisection to compute the exact positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon relative to topocentric surface coordinates from 2026 through 2050.
  • Topographic Horizon Masking: Ingests high-resolution Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA 30 m/pixel Digital Terrain Models (DTMs). Using a 360° radial ray-casting algorithm (1° azimuth steps), it determines the local crater-rim silhouette, computing true physical solar and Earth occlusion without empirical approximations.
  • Dual-Mode 3D Flight Rehearsal: A 3D WebGL engine bridges macro orbital mechanics (trans-lunar injection and lunar orbit) to localized ridge touchdown choreography, casting real-time physical directional shadows across the LOLA terrain mesh based on true topocentric solar elevation.
  • Launch Slip & Decision-Gate Engine: Re-evaluates mission constraints across a multi-day launch delay sweep (-5d to +14d) and four sequential flight milestones (Pre-Launch Hold, Post-Launch TLI, Lunar Orbit Insertion [LOI], and Powered Descent Initiation [PDI]), tracking continuous diurnal battery state-of-charge (SoC) reserves.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Instantaneous "What-If" Analysis: Instead of waiting days or weeks for offline trajectory reruns, mission planners can drag a slider to immediately see how a 3-day or 10-day launch hold alters shadow lengths, surface temperatures, and battery longevity at touchdown.
  • Deterministic & Zero-Hallucination Integrity: Every output is cryptographically signed with a SHA-256 reproducibility hash and verified against 179 automated test suites. No machine-learning hallucinations or fabricated values are used.
  • Zero-Installation Cloud Accessibility: Built as a responsive, precomputed client-side Single Page Application (SPA), allowing anyone—from aerospace engineers to high school students—to run 3D simulations smoothly in any modern browser without specialized hardware or software licenses.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Supporting Artemis & Commercial Landers (CLPS): The lunar south pole has razor-thin operational margins; a launch slip of a few days can plunge an otherwise sunlit ridge crest into cryogenic crater darkness. STELLARON quantifies these landing window tolerances to help safeguard lander survival before departure.
  • Democratizing Mission Design & Education: Complex planetary ephemerides and terrain elevation models have historically been locked behind high-barrier command-line tools. STELLARON translates raw space data into intuitive visual interfaces, inspiring the next generation of lunar explorers, researchers, and students.
  • Open Science Contribution: All code, test suites, and data transformation pipelines are 100% open-source, providing an auditable benchmark for lunar mission analysis.

4. What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Were Used?

  • Planetary & Astrodynamic Data: NASA JPL NAIF SPICE kernels (de421.bsp, naif0012.tls, pck00010.tpc, moon_pa_de421_1900-2050.bpc), LRO LOLA 30m Polar Digital Elevation Models (PDS Geosciences Node).
  • Core Scientific Engine: Python 3.11, SpiceyPy (C-SPICE wrapper), NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio/GDAL (geospatial DTM processing), and Pytest (179 automated test suite).
  • 3D Visualization & Front-End: React 18, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), @react-three/drei, Recharts (telemetry & SoC curves), and Lucide React (space-grade interface icons).
  • Styling & User Experience: Custom CSS design system inspired by mission-control HUDs (Space Grotesk typography, JetBrains Mono data readouts, layered deep-space #05070D glassmorphism).
  • Deployment & CI/CD: Git, GitHub, and Vercel edge deployment with automated SPA routing.

5. How Is the Project Creative?

  • "Game-Controls" 3D Flight Rehearsal: Rather than static graphs, STELLARON models mission progression like a flight simulator—blending orbital space mechanics with local terrain descent where users can orbit freely in 3D, inspect engine plume cutoffs, and watch the physical Sun skim the lunar crater rim.
  • 360° Panoramic Horizon Skyline: Creatively flattens complex 3D spherical trigonometry into an intuitive 2D panoramic silhouette, displaying the apparent 30-day solar oscillation and Earth libration "figure-eight" loop directly against local mountain peaks.
  • 30-Second Built-in Interactive Tour: Features a non-intrusive spotlight tutorial that walks first-time visitors through the interface in 30 seconds with zero barrier to entry.

6. What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Solar Physics & Limb Effects: Evaluated the apparent angular radius of the Sun (0.26∘0.26^\circ0.26∘) and solar constant (1361 W/m21361\text{ W/m}^21361 W/m2) rather than treating the Sun as an infinitesimal point source.
  • Lunar Libration & Direct-to-Earth Communication: Tracked the 6.7° lunar axis tilt and orbital eccentricity that cause Earth to wobble across the polar sky, accurately identifying when mountains sever direct radio line-of-sight.
  • Operational Flight Rules & Conservative Reserve Buffers: Adopted real mission safety margins—defining battery state-of-charge below 20% as a mission failure threshold and 20%–50% as a marginal buffer.
  • Responsible Scientific Labeling: Explicitly labeled all power forecasts and feasibility scores as "(Modelled)" with clear disclaimers, adhering to rigorous NASA scientific communication standards.
